profile.campus: PLAY Katowice Gospodarcza Data Center Campus (DC1/DC2/DC3)
profile.reading:
This is PLAY Centrum Danych DC2 at Gospodarcza 12 in Katowice, Poland, one of two existing buildings in the Katowice Gospodarcza data center complex, operated under the 3S Data Center brand. According to Polish IT trade press, the first building on the site, DC1, opened in May 2011, and DC2 was added on the same plot in 2014. Coverage of a later expansion at the same address puts DC1 and DC2 combined at about 2,200 square meters of floor space, with no public breakdown of how that area splits between the two buildings, so this registry records the combined figure only rather than assigning it to DC2 alone. 3S Data Center subsequently built a third building, DC3, of a further 2,200 square meters at the same Gospodarcza address, described in trade press as Tier 3+ rated and targeted for completion around the first quarter of 2023, which would bring the complex's total footprint toward 4,400 square meters. No source found during this research gave a specific power capacity in megawatts for the DC2 building itself, an honest gap this registry records rather than a guess.

3S Data Center belongs to Grupa 3S, a Polish fiber network and IT infrastructure company that Polish mobile operator Play agreed to acquire from the private equity fund Enterprise Investors, with a preliminary deal signed in June 2019 that trade press reported at 410 million zloty. The acquisition, carried out through Play's parent company P4 sp. z o.o., brought Grupa 3S's roughly 3,800 kilometer fiber network, its data center cluster spanning Warsaw, Krakow, Katowice, and Bytom, and its roughly 2,800 business customers under Play's ownership. Play's stated rationale centered on connecting mobile base stations to owned fiber to support 5G service quality while also gaining a data center and business services arm. P4 held 3S as sole shareholder for several years before formally merging the company into Play's own corporate structure, a step Polish IT press dates to November 30, 2022, following an announcement the previous September. Play's own communications describe the 3S brand as continuing to operate under its existing name and customer contracts after that merger rather than being absorbed and renamed, which is why the DC2 building here still markets and identifies itself as a 3S Data Center facility despite Play now being its ultimate corporate owner.

Play itself changed hands during roughly the same period this facility complex was expanding. French telecom group Iliad announced an agreement in September 2020 to acquire a majority stake in Play Communications for about 2.2 billion euro, and Iliad's own press materials describe a subsequent public tender offer that closed in November 2020 with Iliad holding 96.7 percent of Play's capital and voting rights. Play separately acquired Poland's UPC cable business for about 7 billion zloty, according to Polish trade press coverage of the later 3S merger, adding fixed line infrastructure to the mobile and data center assets already gathered under the same ownership group. No source found during this research ties UPC's acquisition to any specific technical change at the Katowice DC2 site itself, and this registry does not infer one where none was stated.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06 to remove banned aggregator sources (datacentermap.com, Wikipedia) that were present in the prior version of this row. New reading synthesized from datacenterdynamics.com (allowed aggregator), two CRN.pl articles, Play's own press office, ITReseller.pl, and primary Iliad press releases (iliad.fr and globenewswire republication of Iliad's own release) for the Play/Iliad ownership chain. datacentermap.com and cloudscene.com were checked during research for cross reference but excluded as citations per house rules. No power (MW) figure for the DC2 building specifically was found in any source checked, this gap is stated plainly in the reading rather than guessed. DC1/DC2 combined square meterage (2200 sqm) could not be split between the two buildings so is described as a combined figure only, not applied as a per-building numeric fact.
